still_open.problem: The arithmetic part is fixed and pinned, and so is the ${...} part outside double quotes. Inside double quotes the plain-text rule for ${...} is never applied. _read_word's double-quote loop checks only '$(', '$((' and backticks. It ends the quoted string at the first '"', even when that '"' opens a quote nested inside ${...}, which sh, bash, dash and zsh honour. So a quote inside the span still hides its real end, and the rest reads as an unclosed single quote. Three forms parse as one non-opaque vsdd call: 'vsdd survey "${x:-"'"}"$(id)''' runs id in sh, bash 3.2, bash 5.3, dash and zsh; 'vsdd survey "${x:-'"'}"$(id)''' runs it in sh and bash; and 'vsdd survey "${(e):-\$(id)}"' runs it in zsh. A double-quoted setter also feeds a plain-looking reader: 'vsdd survey "${x:=\$(id)}${x@P}"' runs id in bash 5.3, and '"${x:=a[\$(id)]}" ${!x}' or '$((x))' run it in sh and bash. Through the runner, an agent's call in the first four forms got the caller marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput. No test covers these forms.
still_open.proposed_fix: In the double-quote branch of _read_word, on '${', apply _parameter_plain to the text up to the first '}'. With no '}', or with inner text that is not plain, count it as a substitution. Add these to test_shell.py as opaque: 'vsdd survey "${x:-"'"}"$(id)''', 'vsdd survey "${x:-'"'}"$(id)''', 'vsdd survey "${(e):-\$(id)}"' and 'vsdd survey "${x:=\$(id)}"'. Keep 'vsdd survey "${x:-a b}"' judgeable. Add the first form to the agent cases of test_decision_pairing.

still_open.problem: The bracket part is fixed and pinned. But '$[' counts as a substitution only outside double quotes. The double-quote loop does not check '$[', and an escaped '\$' hides the substitution from its character scan. So 'vsdd survey "$[a[\$(id)]]"' parses as one non-opaque vsdd segment, yet runs id under macOS /bin/sh and /bin/bash 3.2, which expand the array subscript a second time. Through the runner, an agent's call got the caller marker, 'allow' and updatedInput. The '$((' form of the same trick is already opaque, because _arithmetic_harmless rejects it.
still_open.proposed_fix: In the double-quote branch of _read_word, count a '$[' as a substitution, as the unquoted branch does. Add 'vsdd survey "$[a[\$(id)]]"' to test_brackets_split_or_are_opaque and to the agent cases of test_decision_pairing.

still_open.problem: Older than this round. _read_word reads $' as a literal '$' followed by a POSIX single-quoted string. bash (including macOS /bin/sh) and zsh read $'...' as ANSI-C quoting, where "\'" does not end the string. So "vsdd survey $'\'' ; id #'" and "vsdd survey $'\'';id;'x'" parse as one non-opaque vsdd call. sh, bash 3.2, bash 5.3 and zsh run id. Through the runner, an agent's call got the caller marker, 'allow' and updatedInput.
still_open.proposed_fix: Count any $' outside double quotes as a substitution, because the shells disagree on where it ends (dash reads it the POSIX way). Add both forms to test_shell.py as opaque, and the first to the agent cases of test_decision_pairing.

still_open.problem: The new _PARAM_PLAIN_CHARS includes '@', so bash 4.4+ ${name@P} reads as plain. @P expands the value as a prompt string, which runs any $(...) in it. Under bash -c, BASH_EXECUTION_STRING holds the command itself. So "vsdd survey '$(id)' ${BASH_EXECUTION_STRING@P}" parses as one non-opaque vsdd call, and bash 5.3 runs the single-quoted $(id), recursing until killed. Inside an eval wrapper it ran the hidden command 966 times in five seconds. Through the runner, an agent's call got the caller marker, 'allow' and updatedInput. '!' (indirect expansion) is on the list too.
still_open.proposed_fix: Drop '@' from _PARAM_PLAIN_CHARS; ${@} then reads as opaque, which is safe. Consider dropping '!' as well. Add "vsdd survey '$(id)' ${BASH_EXECUTION_STRING@P}" and 'vsdd survey ${x@P}' to test_shell.py as opaque, and the first to the agent cases of test_decision_pairing.
